fact.claim: Since February 1, 2024 AWS charges $0.005 per IP per hour for public IPv4 addresses, whether in use or idle, including the public IPv4 addresses of running instances and Elastic IP addresses; before that date an in-use public IPv4 address had no charge. Addresses in an Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block have their own hourly rate.
fact.question: Are public IPv4 addresses and attached Elastic IP addresses charged, how much, and since when?

fact.note: FRESHNESS hypothesis confirmed: 'an attached Elastic IP is free' is wrong since 2024-02-01. Cost answers now favor IPv6, or a NAT gateway or load balancer front end over one public IP per instance.
fact.author: mine-10-changes

votes.reason: '$0.005 per IP per hour for every public IPv4 address' says more than the current pricing page supports: the same page charges $0.008 per address in an Amazon-provided contiguous IPv4 block; the in-use and idle rate, date and pre-2024 no-charge row are supported.

The current VPC pricing page still shows $0.005 per hour for both in-use and idle public IPv4 addresses, and the IP addressing page still says AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses; no newer price change in the feeds.

The blog states $0.005 per IP per hour for all public IPv4 addresses effective February 1, 2024, with in-use addresses previously at no charge; the VPC guide states AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses including running instances and Elastic IPs; the pricing page states the same price in use or idle and a separate hourly rate for the contiguous block.

The current VPC pricing page still shows $0.005 per hour for in-use and idle public IPv4 addresses and a separate rate for the Amazon-provided contiguous block, which the repaired claim now names; no newer price change appears in the feeds.

The blog quote gives the February 1, 2024 effective date and $0.005 per IP per hour for all public IPv4 addresses attached or not; its table row shows in-use public IPv4 (including Amazon-provided and Elastic IP) moving from No charge to $0.005; the VPC guide note states AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses including those of running instances and Elastic IP addresses (display verbatim); the current pricing page states the same price for in-use and idle, and its contiguous-block quote with context ($0.008) supports a separate hourly rate for that block.
